item.title: Getting around: transport
item.description: Commuting, public transport and travel problems in the city.

children.definition: to travel regularly between your home and your work or school
children.example: I commute to the university by metro.

children.definition: the busy time when most people travel to or from work
children.example: The metro is very crowded during rush hour.

children.definition: a long line of cars that cannot move or move very slowly
children.example: We were stuck in a traffic jam for an hour.
The bus was so crowded that I had to stand.

children.definition: the money you pay for a journey by bus, train or taxi
children.example: How much is the taxi fare to the airport?

children.definition: the way that a bus, train or person goes from one place to another
children.example: This bus route goes past the Chorsu Bazaar.

children.definition: a time when something happens later than planned
children.example: There was a thirty-minute delay because of the snow.

children.definition: to be too late to get on a bus, train or plane
children.example: Hurry up or we'll miss the train!

children.definition: the place in a station where you get on and off trains
children.example: The train to Samarkand leaves from platform 2.

children.definition: a person who is travelling in a car, bus, train or plane but is not driving it
children.example: Passengers must show their tickets before they get on.

children.definition: to leave a bus, train or plane
children.example: Get off at the next stop for the museum.
The office is close, so I usually go on foot.
